html:
The most common damage-type on Tibia, since almost all creatures cause it. When you attack with a melee weapon (Axe, Club, Sword) or Distance weapon (Bow, Crossbow, Throwing) and even some spells, you cause physical damage.

This kind of damage is mostly used by Knights and Paladins. Physical damage is affected by the victim's armor value.

The color shown when dealing or receiving physical damage is based on the type of blood (if any) of the creature.

Color Hit Effect Description
Red The color shown for players and most creatures with red blood.
Pale Gray The color shown for undead creatures or certain elementals. Creatures with no blood.
Green The color shown for vermin and insects and other creatures with green blood.
Purple The color shown for constructs, such as Worker Golems. It is meant to represent the energy (electricity) in them.
Orange The color shown for fire based creatures such as Demons or Fire Elementals.
Dark Red The color shown for some creatures such as The End of Days or Lava Creatures.
Dark Purple The color shown for charms Overpower and Overflux.

Spells and Runes

List of spells and runes which inflict Physical Damage.

Spells

Spells that cause physical damage. Note that for Knight Attack Spells (e.g. Berserk, Whirlwind Throw), the damage type depends on the weapon wielded by the caster, so these spells might inflict a portion of magical damage.

Explosion Runes are the only runes left that cause Physical Damage since Winter Update 2007.

Imbuements

The imbuements in Physical Damage work different than with other types of damage. They rise the base skill of the weapon or spells, which increases damage dealt, but not as a fixed percentage as the others. Depending on the profession and weapon, you can raise your Physical Damage with Slash for swords, Bash for clubs, Chop for axes and Precision for Distance Weapons, and all imbuable helmets. Also Epiphany can raise Physical damage in the single case of the Druids' exclusive spell Physical Strike.

Armor Rating

Almost every piece of armor has Armor Rating (Arm:X). The damage reduced is between half the total armor and your total armor minus one, where only pairs of two armor ratings have any effect. So on average Armor Rating blocks a bit less then 0.75 damage... Equipment with high armor rating have been superseded by Physical Protection in most cases.

Physical Protection

Physical Protection is better than Armor rating, because Physical Protection works in percents of the whole damage and is rounded up to a whole number, this means that 1% physical protection always blocks atleast 1 dmg while 1 armor rating has an average of a bit less then 0.75 damage blocked.
1%: 1 dmg received, 1 dmg blocked; 101 dmg received, 2 dmg blocked.
2%: 1 dmg received, 1 dmg blocked; 51 dmg received, 2 dmg blocked.
1%+1%: 2 dmg received, 2 dmg blocked, 102 dmg received, 4 dmg blocked.

Blockade imbuement can lower damage taken by increasing your Shielding, but it does not lower Physical damage taken by fixed percentages. It is still desirable as an addition to your prefered Blocking Set.
